The Kyu camera is a compact device designed to capture 9-second video clips, emphasizing simplicity and the enjoyment of the moment. It features a single button for operation, allowing users to focus on their experiences rather than the act of recording. The camera has a rechargeable battery, a stereo microphone for audio capture, and is water-resistant. Video quality is limited to 1080p resolution at 30 frames per second. On one side, it has a camera lens, and on the other, a 1.6-inch round OLED display with a button underneath for viewing and capturing footage. The device can store up to 27 video clips, and once the storage is full, users can transfer the videos to their smartphone by connecting the camera's USB-C connector. ([wired.com](https://www.wired.com/story/kyu-camera/?utm_source=openai))

The Kyu app complements the camera by automatically stitching together the captured clips into highlight videos, allowing users to relive their memories effortlessly. It operates on an invitation-only basis, enabling private sharing of videos within invited groups. The app is available on iOS and Android devices, with a web browser version in development. Users can record up to 9 clips per day, each 9 seconds long, even without the camera. All memories are automatically saved in the cloud, accessible later at no extra cost. ([wiki.kyu-o.com](https://wiki.kyu-o.com/products/camera/faq?utm_source=openai))

The back of the Kyu camera features a 1.6-inch round OLED display with a button underneath, allowing users to see what they're capturing and to start recordings. This design emphasizes simplicity and ease of use, enabling users to focus on the moment while capturing it. ([wired.com](https://www.wired.com/story/kyu-camera/?utm_source=openai))

For more detailed information, you can refer to the Kyu camera's official page. ([wiki.kyu-o.com](https://wiki.kyu-o.com/camera?utm_source=openai))  No source extracted due to invalid syntax
